assistant.introduction: Check a USDC balance, estimate a payment, or look up a transaction on Arc. Share a wallet address or transaction hash to start. Reads never send a payment.

limits.l1: A mainnet MVP, not a production payment processor.
limits.l2: Memos and references live in the link and the local receipt. They are not written onchain.
limits.l3: History and saved requests are stored in this browser, capped at 200 each.
limits.l4: A request is marked paid only by an exact-amount match found while this app is open. A payment that lands while it is closed for long is not seen, and the requests page prints how far it has looked.
limits.l5: The assistant sends your question, and any address you choose to share, to the AI provider. It has no tool that signs or sends.
limits.l6: Browser tests run against a mock wallet and RPC. They do not prove live settlement.

landing.eyebrow: Sign once · settle in seconds · keep the proof
landing.description: ChaosPay sends USDC on Arc and turns every payment into a record both sides can check on the public explorer. Mainnet USDC has real monetary value.
landing.cap1Title: One currency all the way down
landing.cap1Body: USDC moves and USDC pays the fee. There is no second volatile token to acquire before a payment can go out.
landing.cap2Title: The wallet signs, the app never holds
landing.cap2Body: ChaosPay builds the transfer and hands it to your wallet. No private key, no custody, no account to create.
landing.cap3Title: A request is a URL, or a QR
landing.cap3Body: Recipient, amount, memo and reference travel in the link. Share it as a URL or scan the code — the checkout opens already filled in.
landing.cap4Title: Every payment ends in a receipt
landing.cap4Body: The hash goes straight to ArcScan, and the same payment prints as an invoice your browser can save as a PDF. Both sides check one public record.
landing.cap5Body: Addresses you pay often are saved in this browser under a name, so a transfer starts from a label instead of forty hex characters.
landing.cap7Title: Or trade what you are holding
landing.cap7Body: Swap the Circle stablecoins Arc carries, through Circle own Swap Kit — same chain, one signature, no bridge leg.
landing.cap6Body: It checks a balance, estimates a transfer and looks up a transaction, then shows the evidence with a block number and a check time. It has no tool that signs or sends.
landing.capabilitiesTitle: Everything here is finished. Nothing implied.

docs.faq1A: No. Your wallet signs a direct USDC transfer. ChaosPay has no custody account and no private-key access.
docs.faq2Q: Can I use real money here?
docs.faq2A: Yes. ChaosPay targets Arc mainnet. USDC on Arc has monetary value.
docs.faq3Q: Does ChaosPay charge a service fee?
docs.faq3A: ChaosPay does not add a service fee. Arc charges the network fee in USDC, and your wallet shows the final amount before signing.
docs.faq4Q: Why can a saved request still show unpaid?
docs.faq4A: Request reconciliation scans a bounded range while the app is open. “Unpaid” only means no exact-amount match was found through the block printed on the Requests page.
docs.faq5Q: Are memo and reference stored onchain?
docs.faq5A: No. They travel in the shared URL and local receipt. Only the token transfer and its transaction data are public onchain.
docs.intro: ChaosPay is a non-custodial workspace for sending and requesting USDC on Arc. This reference explains what the app does, what your wallet signs, and which facts can be verified independently.
docs.whatItIs: A browser-based payment interface. It prepares a standard USDC transfer, asks your wallet to sign it, broadcasts it to Arc, and keeps the resulting transaction hash as a receipt.
docs.notProcessor: Payments use the USDC token contract directly. ChaosPay is the interface that prepares and records the transfer; it is not an escrow, bank, or payment processor.
docs.requestBody: A payment request carries the recipient, amount, optional memo, and reference in a shareable checkout URL. The payer can open it without an account and chooses when to connect and sign.
docs.linkCaution: Link contents are readable and editable by whoever holds the URL. Treat the onchain transfer receipt—not the request screen—as proof that funds moved.
docs.settlementBody: The payment screen separates preparation from the irreversible wallet action. Nothing is broadcast until the wallet approves the transaction.
docs.feeBody: At review, ChaosPay estimates gas × gas price with a 20% buffer. The wallet remains the final authority on the fee. If a transaction reverts, the payment fails but a network fee may still be charged.
docs.browserReceiptBody: Useful for people: amount, sender, recipient, memo, reference, fee, status, and hash. It can be printed or saved as PDF and exported as JSON.
docs.onchainReceiptBody: Useful for verification: transaction status, block, token contract, Transfer event, addresses, value, and actual gas used. ArcScan can verify it without trusting ChaosPay.
docs.matchBody: Match the network, token contract, recipient, amount, and successful status. A screenshot or a locally saved memo is not an independent settlement record.
docs.beforeSignBody: Verify the full recipient address, USDC amount, Arc network, and wallet prompt. Blockchain transfers are not reversed by ChaosPay.
docs.constantsNote: These values are imported from the same constants used by the payment code, so the documentation cannot silently describe a different network configuration.
